The remaining wrong-schema case explicitly declares an all-zero digest and expects native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered. Replacing that explicit digest with H1 removes its sole refusal, so the expected REFUSE result cannot remain unchanged even before E2s. It also removes this unknown-digest negative control.

requiredFindings.leadDecision: LD-H10: the retained re-check approach is sound; its blanket each-case digest substitution needs this correction.

Q1.assessment: Exact-digest retained readers fit SS2 and ARS1's separation between selected current sources and retained compatibility. A second reviewed IE:214 exception closes SYN-1/SYN-1F's additive NativeCause gap while preserving I1-L's existing exception. Changing the major alone or rewriting fixture identities would not preserve retained records.

Q2.assessment: H1 and H2 match accepted source bytes, IDs, lengths and carried digests. The other three changed documents are not carried payload-registry documents. Later rows require a reviewed VD2 supersession of the current IE:808 meaning and a corresponding compiled row. VD2 enforces passage lineage; review and HSR-T1 enforce row semantics.

Q3.assessment: Current-only selection belongs at host minting boundaries. Retained joins resolve the record's own exact digest before validation and cardinality. Mixed Runs may reference old and current Coverage IDs; each record retains its own schema declaration. Compiled readers do not replace required retained schema blobs or claim cross-release evaluator semantics.

Q4.assessment: The identity/evaluator sites, host/storage constructors, dormant-row sequence and independent generation-lane boundary are sound. LD-H10's blanket producer-case substitution fails the unchanged-outcome requirement; HSR-RF-01 must be corrected. Future HSR-a/E2s controls and construction timings remain implementation gates, not evidence produced by this review.

Q5.assessment: The three evaluator registry rule strings currently mirror native-v2; E2s must mirror the widened selected sentence as stated. X9 retains the same corpus bytes and synthetic-candidate behavior. This law changes no kill point, driver, custody or recovery rule; later corpus lanes and construction measurements remain owed.
